config.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface

intro.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that displays user profile information, such as a name and age. You will learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define the expected shape of the data (or props) your component receives, ensuring it gets the correct types. This involves writing an interface to specify prop types and then applying it to your component's props. By the end, you'll understand how interfaces help catch errors early and make your components more reliable and easier to understand.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, defining prop types or TypeScript interfaces is essential for building maintainable component libraries and complex interfaces. For example, in dashboard applications, components like data tables, charts, and filter panels receive numerous props that need clear validation—ensuring that a chart component receives the correct data structure for rendering. This practice prevents bugs when teams collaborate on large codebases, such as e-commerce platforms where product cards, shopping carts, and checkout forms must consistently receive valid data. By explicitly defining prop contracts, developers catch errors early during development rather than at runtime, improving reliability in production applications.

objectives: Implement TypeScript interfaces to define prop types for Vue components
Apply prop type validation using the `defineProps` function with TypeScript
Construct reusable component interfaces with required and optional properties
Configure default values for optional props while maintaining type safety
Update existing components to use TypeScript interfaces for prop validation
Bind component props to interface-defined types in template expressions
Integrate TypeScript interfaces across multiple components in a Vue application

steps.title: Define prop types for a user object
steps.instruction: Inside the defineProps function, define a prop object with three properties: name (string), age (number), and isActive (boolean).
steps.hint: Use defineProps with an object where each property specifies its type using the appropriate constructor (String, Number, Boolean).
steps.seedCode:
<script>
// Import Vue and defineProps here
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Add a div element here -->
</template>

<script setup>
defineProps({
  // Define name, age, and isActive props here
})
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have properly typed props for a user object with name, age, and isActive properties.
successCriteria: defineProps is called with an object containing name: String, age: Number, and isActive: Boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all three properties with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using defineProps with an object containing name: String, age: Number, and isActive: Boolean.

steps.title: Add required and default values for props
steps.instruction: In the defineProps configuration, mark the 'name' prop as required and set default values for 'age' (default to 25) and 'isActive' (default to false).
steps.hint: Use the 'required' property for name and 'default' property for age and isActive in the prop definitions.
steps.seedCode:
<script>
// Import Vue and defineProps here
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Add a div element here -->
</template>

<script setup>
defineProps({
  // Define name, age, and isActive props here
  name: {
    type: String,
    required: true
  },
  age: {
    type: Number,
    default: 25
  },
  isActive: {
    type: Boolean,
    default: false
  }
})
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The name prop will be required, while age and isActive will have default values when not provided.
successCriteria: The defineProps configuration includes required: true for name and default values for age (25) and isActive (false).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the required property for name and default values for age and isActive.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've properly configured the prop definitions with required and default properties.

steps.title: Create template to display user data
steps.instruction: Inside the template section, add a <div> element that displays the user's name, age, and active status using the props defined in defineProps.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output prop values in the template. For example, {{ name }} will display the name prop value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the user's name, age, and whether they are active when the component receives props.
successCriteria: The template contains a <div> with three elements that display the name, age, and isActive prop values using {{ }} syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying all three prop values (name, age, and isActive) inside the template using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the prop data correctly. Remember to use double curly braces {{ }} to output the prop values inside the template.

steps.title: Add computed property based on props
steps.instruction: Add a computed property named 'userInfo' that returns a formatted string combining the name, age, and isActive props.
steps.hint: Use the computed function from Vue to create a reactive property that depends on props. Access props directly in the computed function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A computed property 'userInfo' is defined that formats the user props into a descriptive string.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
